page.layout: One printed page: running head at top with page number left; a full-width title line; a framed woodcut engraving in the centre; a verse epigram of four lines below the engraving; a catchword at the lower right. No margin notes.

main_text.head: PECCATA GRASSANTIA.
main_text.p: Infima cum summis miscentur, turpia dictu Facilia facTu nemo est qui pudori habet Inde grauem Ecclypsin Ecclesia, Curia, Priua Patitur.Beatus, ille est qui minimis studet.

page.notes: The engraving (woodcut, framed, no text inside it) shows a central figure in armour standing on a large sphere with a burning candle, flanked by two female figures, one with a sword and scales at the left and one at the right; a draped table below, a pedestal with a skull in a niche, a peacock and a head with a sword at the top. The epigram's third and fourth lines contain some irregular letter forms (long s, the ligature "ft" and "Ecclypsin") that are reproduced as printed. The word "Summa" at the lower right is a catchword.
